topic: The Cosmic Connection: Linking Derivatives and Integrals
target_audience: Advanced High School or First-Year University Students

sections.title: The Grand Paradox: Change vs. Accumulation
lecture_lines: Calculus rests on two main pillars.
Derivatives measure instantaneous change, like velocity.
Integrals measure total accumulation, like distance.
animations: Dash the Cheetah icon [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cheetah.svg] (#FFD700) appears on a horizontal path.
An arrow labeled 'Speed' (#00BFFF) emerges from Dash [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cheetah.svg], showing change.
The path behind Dash [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cheetah.svg] glows green (#00FF00) to show total accumulation.
Text 'Change' and 'Accumulation' appear and pulse in sync.
A gold coin flips showing 'Derivative' and then 'Integral'.

sections.title: Prerequisite Visual: Slopes and Areas
lecture_lines: Geometrically, derivatives represent the slope at a point.
Integrals represent the area under a curve.
One looks microscopically, the other macroscopically.
animations: A curve f(x) (#FFFFFF) appears with a red tangent line (#FF4500).
A magnifying glass [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/magnifying.svg] (#B0C4DE) zooms into the slope of the curve.
A green paint roller [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/roller.svg] (#32CD32) fills the area under the curve.

sections.title: The Inverse Relationship (The Big Reveal)
lecture_lines: Differentiation and integration are actually inverse operations.
They function like addition and subtraction.
Integrating then differentiating returns the original function.
This link is the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus.
It connects the slope and the area.
animations: A grey 'Function Machine' (#A9A9A9) appears in the center.
Input 'f(x)' (#FFFFFF) enters a purple 'Integral Gear' (#DA70D6).
The output then enters an orange 'Derivative Gear' (#FFA500).
The original 'f(x)' (#FFFFFF) exits the machine at the end.
Symbols '∫' and 'd/dx' appear and cancel each other out.

sections.title: Visual Proof: The Accumulation Function
lecture_lines: Define A of x as the accumulated area.
If x moves slightly, area grows by a rectangle.
The rectangle's height is the function's value.
The growth rate is exactly the function's height.
Thus, the derivative of area is the function.
animations: Graph f(t) (#FFFFFF) with a green shaded area A(x) (#00FA9A).
A red vertical bar (#FF0000) at x moves a tiny distance dx.
A thin yellow rectangle (#FFD700) of height f(x) is highlighted.
The change in area 'dA' is shown as height f(x) times dx.
The ratio 'dA/dx' is highlighted as being exactly equal to f(x).

sections.title: The Calculation Shortcut
lecture_lines: We don't need infinite sums to find areas.
Find the antiderivative F whose derivative is f.
The integral is simply the change in F.
Evaluate F at the boundaries b and a.
This shortcut makes complex calculations simple.
animations: Yellow Riemann rectangles (#FFFF00) fill a curve then quickly fade out.
Orange pillars [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/pillar.svg] labeled 'F(a)' and 'F(b)' (#FF8C00) appear at the bounds.
The formula 'F(b) - F(a)' (#FFFFFF) appears, connecting the two pillars.

sections.title: Real-World Application: The Water Tank
lecture_lines: Flow rate is the derivative of volume.
Volume is the integral of flow rate.
Calculus links these two quantities in real-time.

The water level rises as the flow rate meter [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/meter.svg] fluctuations.
A 'Total Liters' counter (#00FF00) updates based on the flow rate.
